notes.title: Improving towns
notes.content:
Towns are intended to provide many benefits during our adventures such as: unlocking new recipes, providing stat boosting hot stew, remedying powerful ailments, and awarding us important quests. It is from here our story and class quests will begin eventually leading us even to other dimensions, where setting up a safe haven will be even more important compared to the quite placid world we start out in. 

Villages and towns (and eventually higher) are not meant to be something we need to set up everywhere we go. Setting up an outpost to help find rare resources in whatever tier we are currently adventuring can be very useful, though it is intended that we only need one "main" town to upgrade and unlock to its full potential.

These are most of the town buildings I am working on, about in the order they are listed. This list does not list the actual upgrades and unlocks per building, and is subject to major change. Some things that are not mentioned here are for example resource storage and transfer capabilities, etc. Still I would love to hear what you think about the concept in general and if there's anything specific you think should be added to the plan in these early stages.

Another topic up for discussion is the placement and construction of the buildings themselves. Currently we are just using a 3x2 house for each of the gatherers which makes it impossible to distinguish them from one another on the outside. I definitely want to give each building it's own look. But for example should we require flattened ground? Should buildings that require a carpenter or stone mason simply have their location assigned by the player and then we have to wait while the carpenter actually builds it using town resources?

notes.title: Now live v 0.3.2
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/8a4a15c7b37077df93766838aab21ff46e6bb2df.jpg[/img]

With v 0.3.2 several new features have been introduced each of which I will go over briefly. For a more complete explanation please read the condensed patch notes.

[h1]Farming[/h1]
Farming brings in several new items: Hoe, Watering Can, Well, and seeds for most harvestable plant types. The process involves, flattening land using terraforming, tilling soil using a hoe, getting seeds from a wild plant, planting seeds in tilled soil, and watering them until they grow. One seed will yield 3 produce, while trees once grown can continue to produce fruit no matter how many times they are picked. Seeds will reduce their tier to match the soil they are planted in if planted in lower tier soil.

[h1]Containers[/h1]
Two forms of containers are now available for crafting: Bag, and Bucket. Buckets, like watering cans can be used to hold and transport water. Currently buckets are bit useless but will be placeable in future updates. Bags can only store stackable items meaning no armor or weapons, facilities, things like that.

[h1]Practice[/h1]
Enchanting and crafting interface now have "practice" buttons on them that allow increased experience gain for crafting without the production of an actual item or enchant. This allows you to level up for example tailoring without having to repeatedly create and destroy clothing just to level up.

[h1]Transmogrification[/h1]
Using a transmogrifier it is now possible to increase and decrease the rarity of resources. For example 1 elite resource can be reduced into 10 rare resources, or 10 rare resources can be increased into 1 elite resource.

Next stop, Town improvements! I've already started working on gatherer NPCs actually gathering resources. After which will be crafting NPCs, guards, merchants, and a long list of Town and Solace improvements.

Thank you again to everyone participating in Early Access, and I'm sorry I haven't done a better job of advertising Solace Crafting.  Nevertheless my dedication has not faltered and I'm very excited to be moving forward with Town and Solace improvements, after which it's on to multiplayer!

[h1]Condensed Patch Notes v 0.3.1a - 0.3.2[/h1]
[b][u]Farming[/u][/b]
- Hoe added to Smithing -> Tools. Cannot be "equipped" but "used" from inventory (for now)
- Use a hoe to till a flat section of land into farmable land
- "Use" seeds to engage planting mode and plant them in tilled soil
- Water soil to make plants grow, or wait for rain (water is free for now)
- Vegetables will grow through germination -> vegetation -> maturity -> old, 900 seconds per stage
- No penalty for "old" plants yet.
- Water will dry up at 1 per 10 seconds

notes.title: Beta Hotfix v 0.3.1a2
notes.content:
I made a mistake in last night's patch that I need to explain a bit so players on the beta branch can understand what kinds of problems it might bring up even after fixing it.

The problem was an unordered enum called ItemType. When an enum is unordered it takes on the value of whatever order it's written in. Because I stuck Hoe and Seeds, two new ItemTypes into the middle of the enum it offset everything behind them. To fix this I have moved Hoe and Seeds to the back of the list, and specifically assigned a number to each entry in the ItemType enum (as it is with all other enum's used in game) so this can't happen again.

However, when an item is saved, it is converted to an integer value, not the text in the code that says "Hoe" or "Consumable". This means that some of the items that were picked up or crafted using last nights patch may continue to think they are something that they are not. I don't expect everyone to remember everything they picked up and crafted in the past 12 hours (on the beta branch only), but if you have food that won't let you eat it, or a hoe or seeds that don't work that's probably why. Best to trash them and find anew.

My apologies for the trouble!

- Fixed out of order ItemType enum

notes.title: Regarding beta v 0.3.0c
notes.content:
I started upgrading several areas of performance with beta v 0.3.0c though was honestly trying to do the bare minimum amount of changes mostly for time constraint reasons. All in all that caused more harm than good and the current beta build is quite unstable.

Since then I have gone forward with more wide-reaching changes changing some of the fundamentals of how game data is managed in runtime. This will lead to increased performance and do away with a number of recurring problems. I have more or less completed the work, but it needs further testing and a few more tweaks and then it should be ready for tomorrow.

Still, this patch will not reduce terrain size, which would force a wipe of all world saves. Currently each terrain is 1 kilometer squared and it's pretty taxing to turn them on and off causing the lagg spikes that occur when running around. The new system will alleviate a lot of that lagg, but not all of it. It would require another one or two arrays of data to be written to disk, but reducing the terrain size to something more like 256 meters squared could end up providing a much smoother gameplay experience. It might be possible to upgrade the world "upgrade" feature to handle that shift and not require a complete wipe as well.

I just don't like leaving the news empty for more than a couple of days at worst and wanted to provide an update on what's going on behind the scenes! Thank you to everyone that has joined us for Early Access, and I hope I haven't caused to many beta tester headaches with the current beta build!

notes.title: Version 0.3 is live!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/c0547445674d58867009aaf2c030d9694763845d.jpg[/img]

Now with boats, crossing that water between you and glory has never been easier! Boats are persistant and can be picked up for ease of use, and are currently the fastest and safest way to travel. We certainly plan to add storage and upgrades and much more to boats over time, and with the new small boat in and working all of that will be much easier when the time comes.

Caves, both cold and hot are also new and very useful. Within caves is the only place to find gem veins making gem hunting now possible in place of gem grinding. Lava caves are the first of several "rare" caves planned, showing up roughly once every ten caves. In almost all cases you will need to build a bridge to make it to the other side of a lava cave should you wish to continue diving deeper.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/041afde4a97f094db896034dc6ad35011ef4310a.jpg[/img]

Caves actually make use of a new system that completely side-steps the above ground terrain generation. Now that this alternative system is in and working, it will be much easier to create side "dimensions" or "pockets" for increasingly varied content beyond just more and more biomes.

Harvesting tools and resource nodes have also had their math reworked into a linear system that is now much more balanced across all levels. For high level players still powering through resources with low level tools, this may come as a surprise. With the new harvesting tool enchants however, it's still very easy to get your harvesting strength well above the toughness rating of equal level resources.

Next up on the todo list:
Farming, fishing, and a number of other water related things.

Thank you again to everyone participating in Early Access, and to everyone making suggestions and reporting bugs both here on the Steam forums and in our Discord server!

For anyone interested in supporting Solace Crafting beyond the purchase of a Steam key, please check us out on [url=https://www.patreon.com/solacecrafting]Patreon[/url]

Lot's more to come!

Note: The windows executable is now "Solace Crafting.exe" instead of SolaceCrafting.exe, a change implement by Unity between 2017 and 2018. Steam has been updated to execute "Solace Crafting.exe." If you receive an executable error Steam may have updated the settings but not the game itself. Restarting Steam should force the update to begin as normal.

Note 2: A known bug in the latest Unity, alt-tabbing destroys cursor lock functionality. This can cause the aim "dummy" to wander with the invisible cursor as opposed to the crosshair (center of the screen) after alt-tabbing from and back to the game and trying to place a facility such as a torch. Unity claims to have fixed the bug in their next release. A restart is required to return functionaly fully in the meantime. Opening the esc menu, or the tab menu will display the mouse letting you reposition it manually as well, though it will still wander while invisible.

The cleaned up list of updates since version 0.2.2 are as follows:

[b][u]Boats[/u][/b]
- Added small boat as a known woodworking facility recipe
- Boats can be picked up using the shift+interact radial menu

[b][u]Caves[/u][/b]

  Uncommon + 5% (base 5% at T1+)

- Added uncommon (1 in 10) lava caves that need to be built across to continue diving deeper
- Lava IS lethal. Inventory items will be dropped on top of lava to make sure they are recoverable.
  
[b][u]Harvesting[/u][/b]
- Adjusted tool rarity damage bonus from 2.5 to 5 per rarity
- Adjusted harvesting passive strength skills from 1 strength per level to 0.2 per level
- Adjusted harvesting strong skills from 4 + 1.5 strength per level to 4 + 0.5 per level

[b][u]Solaces[/u][/b]

notes.title: Beta v 0.2.2h
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/e29f6af6cb53a13aa5c33764be434a4f2c554696.jpg[/img]

Glowing mushrooms are in, adding a much better feel to the caves, the first of many light sources planned. I hoped to be getting crystals and gem veins in today, but there were some bugs that needed attention.

I have reworked the saving and loading pipe a bit to ensure that things execute their timing properly. This should fix a number of small bugs and the not so small bug of sometimes things being overwritten that has unfortunately affected some players over the past few days. Beta branch or not, my sincerest apologies for that.

Yesterdays patch brought in some new tool and resource math as well, though it needed some work and todays patch should help it out quite a bit. Basically a common tool of, for example, tier 20 should provide equal strength for a tier 20 resource assuming your harvesting profession is also up to a level equivalent to tier 20 (100 in this case). That assumes you have bought 20 points speed, and put 20 points into the "strong" harvesting skill for that profession, meaning 60 points in strength. Each higher tier or higher rarity past the minimum will provide an extra +5 per swing. Harvesting enchants will also provide more per swing. This way, a higher level tool with enchants can be used for many levels, while starting out you can still get going with just a tier 0 common tool. Starting out it makes more sense to put points in harvesting strength, then when you have a better tool, buying the strong skill and speed makes more sense.

notes.title: Beta v 0.2.2g
notes.content:
This patch most notably changes tool and resource toughness math. The Strong harvest skills now do more damage per level, but they take up 1 point that would otherwise be spent on basic harvesting strength. This is however now easily counteracted with harvesting enchants. There will probably need to be some tweaking over time, but with the new harvesting enchants I don't think we'll be seeing any problems at higher levels.

There are some good discussions happening on the Steam forums. Most interesting to me is the concept that regular monsters at higher levels don't drop useful loot, and are rarely needed for their experience and light. In other words, they are more a pain in the neck than anything after a certain point. We'd love to hear more opinions on the matter of wandering mobs in the wilds.

notes.title: Beta hotfix v 0.2.2f2
notes.content: Apparently Unity 2018 does not automatically remove spaces from the executable file name making the new executable "Solace Crafting.exe" while Steam has been told it is "SolaceCrafting.exe" as Unity 2017 would remove the space. notes.title: Beta v 0.2.2f
notes.content:
Please backup any worlds you are planning to play, if there's anything in them you can't afford to lose. There may be a rare bug causing terrain files to be overwritten improperly I will be looking into tomorrow.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/ea769597751d33a40d1554b940c53d7307ab1f68.jpg[/img]

This patch upgrades the engine to Unity 2018.2.2 from 2017.1.0. That's a big step and it might have some side-effects for some players. All seems to be working well on my side, but please let me know if an armor set is not rendering, or the sun explodes, something silly like that.

This patch has a number of small fixes and quality improvements, notebly stacking ground and wall torches with the ability to place them from the hotbar now. I also fixed hotkeys not working on the optional 3 hotbars.

Most of all though I've got a "decoration" and resource spawning system for caves working. This is a work in progress in that resources will not yet properly manage their teir as caves aren't fully aware of their difficulty and location in the world yet. This can also cause the temperature to go crazy high if you travel too deep. I will be working on fixing those kinds of numbers and the systems that use them in the next patch.

I have also temporarily doubled the ambient light in caves, and will turn it back down once I get some procedural lights spawning on the walls.

I also turned up the collision detection for players universally. This costs some extra compute power and I haven't finished testing it yet. If you notice a big difference in FPS while moving around compared to before please let me know.

notes.title: Beta v 0.2.2c - Caves!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/db17c68e5ca4aa0209f61fd66ee3d765c8ca7a47.jpg[/img]

Caves are in! But only just! This is the absolute first wave of spelunking and only incoporates the cave generation, transportation, saving and loading, and so forth. There are no minerals, monsters, traps, nor special rooms to be found down in the caves yet!

In short, Solace Crafting up until now has been entirely based on terrain management. Where you are, what's there, how's the weather, all of these things no longer matter underground, but the same systems all have to be maintained and work nonetheless. For example building, dropping items on the ground, teleporting across long distances. There are a lot of things that are moving and hopefully not running into each other in the background and getting all of those to work properly with an entirely different system is not that easy.

Having said that, things look to be working well. Caves will only appear on new chunks! Chunk sizes are 8km x 8km. That means you may need to travel out a bit somewhere new before you see any. They will show up on the map just like towers do. Or you can always start a new world. If anything goes wrong you can always recall or use the /stuck command to return to the surface. For that purpose I would suggest that you do not set your home solace to an underground solace (yet). Though backing up your main world is always a good idea.

Some caves are long and skinny, some are big and fat, and there are some things that I'm aware of:
- Caves always go downward, and they always go West. This is temporary.
- There is only one texture being plastered onto everything. This is temporary.
- The camera tends to bleed through the floor when touching it letting you see through the walls. I will fix this.
- Torches do not stack, and I don't think they work from the hotbar. These I will change so they do/can.
- Ladders are needed to go backwards at some points where starting a whole new structure isn't really worth it. I will implement this.
- Caves do not currently shift for floating precision correction. Meaning it is possible to travel so far that things will start to jitter (10-20km+)

Gem veins, lava, traps, and some new monsters are planned as well as some hand-made rooms, as well as procedural dungeons made of brick and other "man"-made structures. Any other ideas/needs?

In the morning I am leaving town for a few days to celebrate my sister-in-laws wedding overseas, and will not be able to patch anything new until I get back. I will check the Steam forums and our Discord channel at night. I hope that despite the lack of decoration, everyone likes the new cave system and can see somewhat where I'm going with it!

notes.title: Incoming skills
notes.content:
The past two days I've been upgrading skills to a much better system.

Skills themselves are now handled using a Unity type called a scriptable object. Rather than writing a script for each skill, the scriptable object approach lets us define the skills settings on a single asset and let the system handle the rest. In other words I can copy and paste an ice spell, rename is to ice2, up the damage, and it's good to go in 5-10 seconds. Of course we want our skills to have different names, icons, effects, and so forth, but the system is really that easy now that it's all setup and working.

To go with that, I have upgraded the skill unlock interface so that almost everything is now automatic. This is important for how many skills I plan to get into the game over time, but also for mod support. This way anyone with a copy of Unity (which is free) can download a script package I will make available in the future, create some skills, and just putting them in the right folder will make them accessible in-game.

Generally most skills will fall into one of several categories: single target, projectile, aoe, buff, heal, etc. There are a few expections however such as the basic attack skill or strong harvest skills which check to see what you are weilding or what you are harvesting and performs the appropriate action. Setting up these special cases has used up all my time for today, but I'm hoping to get at least 10-20 new skills in tomorrow. Just wanted to chime in rather than let another silent night go by.

Looking forward to lightning and explosions!

The Great Rebalance!

Combat and equipment math prior to todays patch had several serious flaws with it. Todays patch seeks to remedy those problems and make things much easier to tweak and tune over time. This is the first step to adding in more skills.

Several important changes simplified:
- Medium armor will generally take 100% damage. Heavy armor can offer generally up to around 50% damage reduction. Light armor tends to take around 150% damage. No armor can cause a player to take up to 600% normal monster damage. Please don't run around naked at night.

- Medium skills (Scout and Disciple) will generally do around 100% base skill damage. Heavy skills (Squire) will generally do around 60% base skill damage. Light skills (Apprentice) will generally do around 140% base skill damage. These are of course subject to balance over the next few days of testing.

- Medium and heavy armor penalties to healing and magic are temporarily off and will be back tomorrow.

- This new system no longer stores armor, damage, and speed directly on equipment. That means that once equipment has been upgraded (brought into the new version) it will no longer be useable in older versions. Please back up your files if you plan to play on both the beta and the live branch.

notes.title: Version 0.2.0j now live!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/2b567e0a2d7dd66cc20c5deaa31320d5a76945bf.jpg[/img]

Now live on the default build, version 0.2.0 brings in a lot of new features, as well as a complete rework of world generation. With each new development branch I try to find a balance between new content and improvements. This build includes several changes to my development workflow, increasing productivity, and making it much easier to add in more encounters or points of interest in the near future.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/5ada6970cb55ff1523e9bc83bcb4d3f897321d63.jpg[/img]

The new desert biome is the only "brand new" biome, though ocean, mountain, and grass biomes have also received a lot of attention. These biomes are intended to each be a source of different animals and plants for cooking and alchemy in the coming weeks. In the grass biome for example we now have lemon and orange trees, that once picked will regrow their fruit after two days in-game. This mechanism will also help with farming and the harvesting of crops in future updates.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/0b04f376da0edf3531f5548e4e0704ba6a75cc5d.jpg[/img]

In order to allow further options than just "harvest," I've added a "radial," or secondary action menu to harvestables via shift+interact. This allows you to choose for example, harvesting an orange tree for oranges, or chopping it down for wood.

Because of the scanning features added in recently I've also added a "harvest essence" option to uncommon+ resources. This allows you to guarantee being rewarded an essence, at the cost of destroying the node.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/27fd9c5b5164d69b9a82ffd3f97996239f0ff4a8.jpg[/img]

One problem with changing world generation in any game is that it usually requires us to start fresh. To cope with this I've added in two new features: world updating, and ley line teleporters.

World updating will scan through a saved world's files and mark all structures and solaces for repositioning. This way even though a lake may have turned into a desert and an open field into a mountain, the game will automatically attempt to adjust the placement of all player built structures. Unfortunately it does not guarantee that your house won't end up half inside of a steep hill, but it will keep them out of water, and is a better alternative than starting over completely in most cases.

Ley line teleporters were added in to ease the burden of travelling back out to distant locations in the event that a high level character chooses to start a new world. They are limited to the four directions of north, east, south, and west, but can send a player up to 100km away provided you've got the rare stone required to upgrade them.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/15c0c8329c63456de51391b4bf8cce1f6f022ed3.jpg[/img]

Seven different armor sets were also added in as possible drops from fire elementals. Over the next few weeks I hope to be adding in a lot more content in the form of weapons, potions, enchants, skills, and cosmetic items, as the majority of the "base" systems are in and working.

Solace Crafting has certainly come a long way in just four months of full-time development, though there is still a lot to do! I am going to be working on a new video starting tomorrow and will be running a modest marketing campaign over the next few weeks in hopes of raising enough money to hire additional help. I have grown into a decent programmer, though am still far from becoming an expert.

A big thank you to everyone on [url=https://www.patreon.com/solacecrafting]Patreon[/url] supporting development monetarily. It makes a big difference, and I hope I'm able to attract more support in the coming weeks. Patreon support starts as low as 1$/month and can add up to a major source or funding!

notes.title: Beta v 0.2.0f
notes.content:
This update combines the encounter (points of interest) management system directly into the terrain generation so that terrain can be flattened nicely for encounters added in from here on, and to create "safety" zones to prevent the spawning of resources inside of towers and big rocks getting too close to towers, for example.

While working on the terrain generation I also made some changes to improve tree placement and unintended shallow water areas. These changes all in all require a world "wipe" or starting a new world, however...

Now with a world "update" feature! Even in the event of new content and/or world generation algorithms that require starting a new world, this feature will mark all of the player created structures so that they realign themselves with the new world when they are re-encountered. This is an imprecise science unfortunately, and it's still entirely possible to end up with half of your house inside of a hill, or in the middle of a lake, though I have set it up so that things won't go underwater and we can improve the system further over time.

Just in case, there is now also a "backup" button on each world that will copy the entire world.

This was a lot of work under the hood, and may still have a hitch or two in it. All in all this improves my work flow quite a bit, and I can add new encounters from here on much easier.

notes.title: Beta v 0.1.09j
notes.content:
Backpacks! Running out of storage space sucks, and now that should be less of a problem. Backpacks can add up to 20 inventory slots at +5 slots +2 per tier. Storage chests can now also be upgraded and colored.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/9b36d5466f099b5b6a6b1873a5a8a467736cbf0e.jpg[/img]

Coloring is in not only for storage chests, but for all armor types as well. There isn't a preview feature yet, so it's a bit touch and feel, but I love personalization!

The increased storage is by no means a final answer to the ongoing problem of too many resources x tiers x rarities + essences + gems, and so on. I believe a non-slot based system is a better answer than just adding more and more slots. Something more like a magical ore storing void pocket that can store and sort up to x number of any kind of ore. Or a feature that has been planned for a long time, a way to send things back to your solace storage, coupled with craftable storage extensions for each resource. Let me know what you think.

I'm going to be working on polishing the map and resource management tomorrow. Now that we know where rare materials are supposed to be, players are finding they aren't always there. It seems reloading the world brings them in properly, until I found out what's wrong.

notes.title: Beta v 0.1.09h
notes.content:
I've added the start of the Town interface, something intended to grow quite a bit and be a central part of the game. This will only populate its details if you are within power range of a solace, the heart of any town.

Getting town buildings and their citizens to communicate properly with one another as well as the new interface required changing the way they are all generated, saved, and reloaded in the game world meaning citizens summoned prior to this patch will no longer be present, and unfortunately those buildings are going to be stuck, for now. I have an idea for tomorrow on changing another minor system so we can get them out of our current worlds, but any newly built buildings and citizens will connect properly with the new system so we can use the "Remove Building" button to get rid of them if we so choose. Keep in mind this will not wipe any upgrades you have made to resource scanning, and summoning a new miner (for example) will let you continue to upgrade ore scanning if you were not yet level 4 on a particular solace.

In truth, I spent most of this week working on a custom solution to the lagg spikes we currently have when a new terrain "turns on" in the game world. It's something all large open world Unity based games are forced into at one time or another. However, working by myself, with still so much content I'm rushing to get in before starting to market Solace Crafting for profit enough to hire help, I'm putting the tools down until more help is acquired. It's not that I can't do it, but it will take weeks and I don't believe the benefits it will bring outweigh the lull in development it would create at this point in time.

I want guards that you can equip, and better solace upgrade fights! Farming, alchemy, and more biomes! We'll get fancy with a custom engine after more of these things are realized.

notes.title: Mid-week update
notes.content:
Fellow adventurers! I was trying to wrap up the next patch, but it's still got a couple things I need to fix up before publishing. Instead I wanted to give a little update rather than let too many days of silence pass. There is a number of new things coming in most likely tomorrow.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/76eace28d59117245f3585b766b53f2247d8ffb1.jpg[/img]

Obelisks have a new model along with a visible attack, albeit quite simple for now. I'll be changing the colors and adding particle effects and attacks based on the different types of obelisks that should be in soon.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/c79994eb4455741217c80d5e2f868846257a61cc.jpg[/img]

The first NPC, the Logger, is making their way in. I'll be honest the males are quite reluctant to put their clothes on, that's one of the things I'm still patching up, but these guys and gals are intended for a number utilities. For starters they will allow us to upgrade our solaces with resource scanning capabilities. Resource scanning will make use of a new map feature to show where rare resource are within scanning range of the solace. The scanning range upgrades are tentatively a radius of 500m, 1,250m, 2,500m, and 4,000m. There will be a specialist for each resource type. Once the logger is in and working well, the rest will be easier to add in.
You can see in the picture a couple of new items I added in for the Logger, a bed, and a woodpile (previously seen with the old towers). Beds are craftable, and both can be picked up and placed.

This week is "golden week" here in Japan, with a string of holidays. I will be out of town Friday and Saturday, so am looking forward to patching tomorrow (Thursday).

Best wishes! And thank you to everyone participating in early access and the ongoing discussions here on the Steam forums and in our discord channel as well.

notes.title: Beta v 0.1.09c
notes.content:
Up until now the map was being handled via a single file that over time has proven to create a problem with saving and loading. To deal with this I've created a separate Map folder within each world folder that will save each tile individually. I'm research some other ways to go about things, but this is a fair and easy start. This way a file will only be created once, and files will only be loaded off the disk during world load.

This patch also brings in the first set of recipes that you can find out in the world. A new player will not start out knowing the mage armor cloth set, but can find them as drops off of fire elementals. This is mostly in at this stage for testing to be sure the mechanisms all are working so we can add more weapons and armor and enchants via leveling up, and adventuring, instead of just knowing everything from the beginning.

Worlds will also now save a current position for each player that enters them. This will cause a one-time reset of all current saved locations, sending players back to the broken solace regardless of where they last saved. I hope that doesn't cause anyone too much grief!

notes.title: Weekly Update #11
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/71cc0ddb47f66179203381d20e0d110174a66de8.jpg[/img]
The current build live on both the main and the beta builds is working quite well! There is still a "zombie" bug where players die, but don't actually die and get stuck where they are, but I was able to finally reproduce it and fix it for next patch.

The past couple days I have been, somewhat regrettably, stripping out the current 3rd party vegetation management system and implementing a custom solution in it's place. I'm still working on improving the grass, as you can see in the picture. The main reason I went with the 3rd party solution in the first place was actually because the grass looks so much better... But it caused frequent spikes when turning, was difficult to manage, very hard on the GPU (video card), and was really making it difficult to plan a map system that I hope to start working on soon.

We lose our fancy grass (for now), but we gain performance, and above all increased customization options. I can now add sliders for "resource render distance," "grass render distance," etc. Perhaps the most player friendly option this makes easier for me is a magical slider we could implement called the "sparkly render distance." Under the current system sparkly particles are used to show rare resources throughout the game world. We can turn them up as far as we like now, though hopefully the mapping system and some fun town options coming soon will provide more attractive ways to find rare resources than aimless wandering.

It's warmed up to a very nice Spring temperature here in central Japan. I hope everyone is happy and healthy wherever you may be reading this from!

notes.title: Patch v 0.1.07l
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/661d05446d636dc83d5de4dba662347d1cdb0f78.jpg[/img]

This patch is going live to both the beta and the live build, bringing in saving and loading of structures, monoliths, larger building types, and lots of little fixes.
[b][u]Note that this will require starting a new world for players on the live build.[/u][/b]
The most recent patch notes are as follows:

v 0.1.07l - 2018.04.03
- Fine tuned the compass as it was a little off
- Fixed pig graphical error
- Fixed pig harvesting error
- Fixed new soul creation going back to the start screen at night
- Added reset buttons to the six categories of character creation
- Added rarity borders and "T0" text to interactable inventory slots (storage chests, refining station, enchanting table, etc)
- Added rarity wording to item details in the inventory, "Uncommon" etc.
- Increased base damage of non-stone weapons by 0.5
- Fixed a bug related to monster audio
- Added experience and light rewards to monoliths

The complete list of changes to the live build, besides those above are as follows:

v 0.1.07 - 0.1.07k
- Reworked save game files to a more performant, smaller structure
- Turned off occlusion culling
- Updated pig and monster LOD management to a better system
- Fixed a bug that would load players naked in an empty level after returning to the start menu and going back into a world
- Fixed cloud settings not loading properly
- Monoliths now spawn up to 25 per terrain
- Monoliths are now spread out "evenly"
- Monoliths can now spawn anywhere beyond the first 200m
- Added a lower end version of clouds
- Increased sky performance in general
- Tuned clouds and wind for each weather type
- Setup fog for each weather type
- Fixed invisible pigs
- Added elemental LODs
- Improved pig LODs
- Improved monster/pig occlusion culling
- Improved monster/pig animation culling
- Fixed monolith guard locations saving improperly, causing them to not reload. This will fix current worlds.
- Added dynamic occlusion culling to monoliths and monsters
- Added a simple compass
- Changed rarity node spawn math. All five resource types should be more even now with roughly
  5 uncommon per terrain (1024m^2) (per resource) (starting level 5)
  1 rare per two terrains (starting level 15)
  1 elite per ten terrains (starting level twenty)
  1 legendary per fifty terrains (starting level thirty)
  Spawn rates are reduced beneath the listed "starting level".
- Fixed an error not saving resources properly
- Fixed a variety of errors related to "encounter" (tower and monolith) storage causing them to not spawn properly in several cases
- Monolith spawn rate increased 5 fold
- Monolith champion spawn chance raised from 5% to 50%
- Cleared monoliths will no longer reset on reload
- Monolith data is now stored on generation, meaning if there is a champion there will always be a champion until cleared, and a cleared monolith will retain its inventory if, for example, you can't pick it up right away
- Fixed loading structures reporting "not enough resources" improperly
- Fixed loaded structures all assuming they are on terrain 0,0 which caused bugs for solaces placed on loaded structures
- Item rewards will now color overlay messages matching their rarity
- The starter platform is now selectable for building. The original building pieces are locked, though can be added on to. This will only work in new world.
- Fixed WoodStairsL bug and collision issues
- Fixed the skills "Upgrade" button not turning off when no skill/attribute is selected which was causing errors
- Added simple text tooltips to the building interface
- Improved audio performance
- Improved building rendering performance
- Fixed mid-drag items/skills from staying open after closing the inventory interface
- Updated wall torch and ground torch models
- Wall torches will now automatically rotate to fit what you are attaching them to
- Increased torch light intensity 150%
- Fixed light bleeding through most buildings
- Ground torches are now placeable on ground
- Eaten items will no longer leave their details up in the inventory if none remain
- Fixed an error when trying to select a building by clicking on a door or shutter
- Fixed uncommon monoliths not spawning gems, only resources
- Fixed facility and structure placement clicks going through the interface
- Fixed loading structures not working properly with tiered and/or rare materials
- Fixed and error causing terrains touching the North to South or East to West borders to spawn zero encounters
- Moved the intractable display beneath all other windows
- Added a check on tooltips to turn them off if their source is no longer visible
- Improved defense, dodge, block, parry, and resist calculations to use a diminishing returns formula based on the monsters level (needs testing)
- Added compatibility for blocked building pieces during rotated placement of loaded structures
- Fixed a number of bugs with the new large buildings
- Added 2 new building pieces, stone round floor small and medium (bit of a texture issue with them I'm still playing with)
- Started implementing monster loot tables
- Added the first "small encounter." They look like stone monoliths and are guarded by 2-3 elementals. Each elemental has a chance to be a champion. If there is a champion the loot quality will be increased to uncommon. If one guard is attacked, all guards will respond as a group.
- Fixed the building recipe list not sizing properly
- Changed the building recipe list to only scroll up when a new slot type is manually selected
- Changed weapon tiers and rarities to give equal speed bonuses for 1H and 2H weapons instead of double the bonus to 2H
- Added a building blocking system where large building pieces can now block other pieces. Blocked slots will show as red on the building selection interface, unless selected which they are then green. If selected the recipe list will show a description that it is blocked, what by, and give you the option to select that piece in case you want to deconstruct it.
- Added 2 more building pieces
- Fixed a memory leak involving facility placement
- Fixed facilities not changing colors during proper / improper placement locations
- Fixed not all parts of some facilities going translucent during placement
- Fixed problems with loading structures that have been rotated off the original rotation during placement. This will automatically fix any already placed structures that are currently bugged, but will not remedy extra pieces that were placed "improperly" due to the bug.
- Renamed some of the stairs because there are so many kinds now, though it should not affect saving/loading
- Added 11 more building pieces
- Updated font descriptions
- Fixed common enchants giving 0 stats during enchanting
- Fixed uncommon+ enchants giving less stats than intended during enchanting
- Fixed higher rarity weapons being slower instead of faster during crafting
- Fixed a weapon damage math error during crafting
- Fixed an armor math error during crafting
- Fixed demons not taking damage
- Fixed an error in saved structure piece counting
- Fixed a solace beacon positioning bug
- Set the crafting interface recipe list to automatically scroll to the top after profession/category selection changes
- Added 26 building pieces
- Building rotation now properly shows a dummy using only the South and East edges. A North edge is the South edge of the next piece North, for example. Without this halves and quarters do not display properly. With this a South / West half wall will always be on the South or West side despite being rotated what feels like around the Y axis. If this is too counter-intuitive I will make halves and quarters swap with one another depending on the selection.
- Added save and load buttons to the structure panel in the building interface. saving a structure will store all buildings and facilities placed within the structure to a file, but not the contents of any facilities, nor any placed solaces. Loading will then allow a user to place a saved structure for the same cost required to build it anew. As with building, the Q and E keys (the default bindings) can raise and lower a structure, and Z and C can rotate. There is one "Premade" structure included for testing purposes.
- Note that the Broken Solace at the start has no power and so cannot "use network storage" when building
- Hitting cancel on the New Structure interface will now stop placement selection instead of returning to it
- New structure / building selection will no longer click through the interface

You may need to restart Steam for the update to begin.

notes.title: Weekly Update #10
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/e92b763c4320eba6a1011f83492bae4760f649eb.jpg[/img]

I was hoping to get in the first medium encounter this week along with more buildings, but turning the small encounter count way up led to a massive increase in monsters, bringing up two major flaws in the game.

For one, the rock elementals which are skinned meshes, that is, mesh rigged with bones for animation, were too costly with tons of them on screen all at once. This has been remedied in tomorrow's patch using a more performant form of LOD grouping, which decreases their details the further they are from the camera. This is the first of two steps, the other being runtime batching of multiple elementals into a single render instead of each individually, but that will require a bit more work later on.

Secondly, we were saving data in all sorts of different kinds of files, each for a specific type of data. This way easy for me to manage early on, but it had a couple of problems. For one, encounter data, which includes the new monoliths, was being saved per world, instead of per "section" or "terrain". That meant that the further you traveled the bigger and bigger that data pool was growing and every-time a save was triggered it had to rewrite the entire file, often over 100mb. Now it is per terrain, only for terrains you have loaded into the world, much lighter, and compressed after saving, usually around 15-30kb when combined with resource data and others.

While working on optimizations I did a lot of system measurements and still, by far, the most performance consuming aspects of the game are the clouds and the vegetation. This week I implemented a second lower end cloud system for each weather type and reworked fog while I was in there. The new option to turn off volumetric clouds can make a big difference in FPS on some machines, so give it a try! There is currently a bug where the cloud settings are not reloading properly I hope to address tomorrow.

There is another small bug left with the current build that I hope to finish up tomorrow and publish! Once things are running faster than ever, I'll be back on track looking to turn our currently inaccessible towers into monster filled treasure packs!

Thank you to everyone participating in early access, and special thanks to everyone participating in the beta builds, it's been a bumpy week!

Oclusion culling is one of those unfortunate things that procedural Unity does not like. It's a bit of a brute force, albeit simple, custom solution, but it should help with performance a bit now, and increasingly so as we bring more content in.

I tried implemented a different sky system today (not in this patch), and while definitely not as gorgeous, the performance difference is very real. This patch fixes several major bugs related mostly to long distance encounter management, structure placement, and resources. It also revisits one part of rarity math, though other points are to be addressed and or added in over the coming days. There were some pretty nasty bugs in there, past 8km, I'm sorry I didn't see them sooner.

- Changed rarity node spawn math. All five resource types should be more even now with roughly
  5 uncommon per terrain (1024m^2) (per resource) (starting level 5)
  1 rare per two terrains (starting level 15)
  1 elite per ten terrains (starting level twenty)
  1 legendary per fifty terrains (starting level thirty)
  Spawn rates are reduced beneath the listed "starting level".
- Fixed an error not saving resources properly
- Fixed a variety of errors related to "encounter" (tower and monolith) storage causing them to not spawn properly in several cases
- Monolith spawn rate increased 5 fold
- Monolith champion spawn chance raised from 5% to 50%
- Cleared monoliths will no longer reset on reload
- Monolith data is now stored on generation, meaning if there is a champion there will always be a champion until cleared, and a cleared monolith will retain its inventory if, for example, you can't pick it up right away
- Fixed loading structures reporting "not enough resources" improperly
- Fixed loaded structures all assuming they are on terrain 0,0 which caused bugs for solaces placed on loaded structures
- Item rewards will now color overlay messages matching their rarity

You may need to restart Steam for the update to begin.

notes.title: Weekly Update #9 - 2018.03.21
notes.content:
The results of the survey are in! Thank you to everyone that participated in the survey. Please understand that the survey was not intended to make me drop everything and do what it says, but for me to get a better understanding of what players feel is most lacking in the current version. All of the systems are interconnected and there are certain things that definitely need to be improved and/or incorporated before we dive head first into some of the topics.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/36b62875a3b37aa2a8ed45f25516f6256393b4ab.jpg[/img]

I think it's quite clear that everyone, myself included, is most interested in more things to do. In light of that I spent the last week improving the building system in a number of ways and adding in a variety of new buildings. The main purpose for this being that I want to make everything in-game manipulatable by players, rather than off-limits areas and/or no-build zones all over the place. For example a large castle full of monsters and loot should be able to be conquered and secured, though perhaps not easily, and then handed over to players to control, deconstruct, or build upon. Part of the way that NPC towns are planned to work has always involved this, asking players to repair things, build things, defend things, and ultimately rewarding them in a variety of ways.

One of the biggest shortcomings of the building system as I saw it, was it's inability to handle larger pieces. Just now published in Beta v 0.1.07d we now have that capability, albeit only with one recipe for today, letting me start to put in bigger and more unique pieces so that I can start building points of interest throughout the world. Now that the structure saving system is in and working it's also possible for players to construct buildings, post them on the forums, and get them included in-game! Ultimately I hope to make this possible with just about everything in-game through Steam Workshop.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/fea2f7ec1884c5d1578fc67b919b23e30093e708.jpg[/img]

Alongside points of interest I'm also working on the first few town buildings for player towns. The new larger building pieces use a system of blocking off areas that they are "taking up," as in the picture above, which will also work well for placing special items unique to town buildings like a sawmill for example. The first wave of town buildings are intended to make creating towns a very beneficial process, though still quite simple, if you're only looking to place down pre-made structures and unlock the benefits.

Thank you to everyone participating in early access! I know it's been a lot of mostly bug fixes and usability improvements since we started, which aren't really very "fun." I'm looking forward to getting more and more content in from here on as we improve upon our now much more solid foundation!

I also have to be honest and point out that there was no weekly update #8! The weekly updates were slowly pushed back a day at a time as I waited each week for things just around the corner. Eventually I was a whole week behind, and I apologize. I hope to just post a status update somewhere mid-week each week regardless of whenever the next best thing may be.

Best wishes!

[url=https://www.patreon.com/posts/17685233]View on Patreon[/url]

notes.title: Live branch updated to v 0.1.06d
notes.content:
There are quite a few fixes and upgrade that had not yet been pushed to the live branch, so I am pushing it to the most recent build 0.1.06d. The biggest changes being improved pathfinding and monster AI as well as reworked combat math.

Note that some items crafted after the patch may be stronger or weaker than similar items crafted after the patch. The alternative, making everyone start over from scratch, is something I prefer to avoid as much as possible.

The complete list of changes are as follows:

v 0.1.05c -> v 0.1.06d
- Fixed torches not being able to be crafted with tier 1+ wood
- Updated player stat calculations (see below)
- The in-game attribute descriptions are not yet updated!
- Attribute points now award a full attribute instead of one quarter
- Players now receive +5 health, +3 energy, and +3 mana per level as well as +0.2 health regen per 10s per level
- Melee skills now do 10% less damage (but allow heavy armor)
- Magic skill snow do 10% more damage (but require light armor to do full damage)
- Two-handed weapons now do 125% dps one-handed weapons
- The tier and rarity of weapons now properly increase dps via both speed and damage, not just damage
- Block checks no longer occur unless a shield is equipped
- Changed enchantment math as well
- Fixed pathfinding not updating realtime with newly placed buildings
- Fixed crashing bug/terrains not loading (caused by multiple pathfinding obstacles on a single object)
- Improved pathfinding obstacles. Monsters and animals should now properly avoid all trees and things
- Fixed autorun keybinding / display errors
- Fixed enchanting "slots required" going negative
- Essences and gems are now "common" items (white/rarity 0)
- Essences now drop via the uncommon loot table (1 in 100)
- Ore now makes two rolls on the uncommon loot table whenever an uncommon drop occurs (gems, essences, uncommon ore) because the loot table is much bigger than other resources
- Fixed mining speed and skinning speed interfering with each other
- Changed "10" hotkey to "-"
- Fixed hotkey "-" not loading/refreshing properly
- Halved shortbow speed and damage
- Fixed buildings capped at tier 11
- Changed harvesting experience required to level to from 50 to:
  Level 0 = 5
  Level 1 = 10
  Level 2 = 15
  Level 3 = 20
  Level 4 = 25
  Level 5+ = 25 + (level within tier 0-4)
- Removed "chance to stun" and "slowing movement speed" shield bash and stomp until fixed
- Changed max stack size from 99 to 100 because 99 is annoying XD
- Monsters and animals will no longer spawn within 30m of the player or player built buildings
- Fixed monsters running through stumps (except the big long one on its side)
- Completely upgraded pathfinding system
- Completely reworked mob spawning system
- Can now walk on resources and stumps
- Fixed a bug related to long distance teleporting
- Changed obelisk sensing collider to a 0.5s sphere check
- Fixed holding down attack not working
- Added autorun key (default is R )
- Pigs will now grant bonus meat on the last harvest
- Crafting and harvesting experience is now measured using non-whole numbers. Resources 3 or more tiers lower than your current profession level for said resource will grant no experience while 1 and 2 tiers under will grant reduced experience. Likewise resources tiered higher than your current profession level for said resource will grant increased experience. This shift will reset the experience at your current level for all professions, but not your profession levels.
- Crafting with and harvesting rare resources now grant increased experience per level of rarity
- Enchanting is no longer 5+ enchants per level, but grants 10 exp per basic enchant at equal tier, giving more or less the same results along with all of the new benefits applied to all professions and the way they gain experience
- Improved storm and heavy rain sound loops
- Enabled hardware mouse
- Fixed bad string in enchanting interface
- Fixed enchanting not leveling up properly
- Gave stone foundations a proper PBR texture
- Improved solace and solace beacon shader to render fog and glow at night
- Fixed several terraforming bugs
- Fixed grass not moving with terraforming
- Rain will no longer fall through buildings
- Fixed some solace upgrade interface bugs. Perhaps not all of them
- Fixed door animations

notes.title: Weekly Update #7 - 2018.03.11 / March 2018 Development Survey
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/235e86f20a178683c4890df93586b284013ceced.jpg[/img]

With the new pathfinding in and working despite a small bug or two still to be addressed, I have started working on adding some new features in. First up and already well on its way is building (structure) saving and loading. This is being worked on largely for two reasons. One being Steam Workshop integration which may still be a ways away, but is ultimately something I hope to integrate heavily into crafting, building, quests, points of interest, avatars, even voice packs, cooking recipes, the more the better! The other main reason being to give NPCs (non-player characters) a quick place to live.
In the near future I will set things up so that players can design and build their own structures to house NPCs, but getting preset buildings in is a necessity for Steam Workshop integration anyway, and an easy way to be sure that a building is "complete" enough to house whoever we're summoning.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/2508333e05d4208f8b764ecbd1103ff42d3f3fef.jpg[/img]

In order to be sure that I don't just run off and develop whatever is it I like, I've setup a short 1 minute survey to help me better judge what it is our community it looking forward to over the next few weeks. I will try to run a short survey like this every once in a while, and would appreciate it if you've got the minute to fill it out!

[url=https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/PMY6CXZ]Solace Crafting - March 2018 Development Survey[/url]

Thank you!

notes.title: Beat v 0.1.06d
notes.content:
In this patch I updated player attributes, level bonuses, and skill damages to better align with monster health and damage math. This is not the final product by any means. For one, item enchants are largely being ignored in the math at this point. All-in-all it's made higher level mobs much easier, so long as you wearing appropriate gear. I only tested up to level 50, I know some players are higher, but it might actually be too easy for now.

It'd be fun here to add some more utility skills like slow to ice, stuns, etc., but we really need to get some more town and building aspects off the drawing board and in-game.

notes.title: Beta v 0.1.06
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/5439ee833dbb97fa39801d877bc01c8a6cf34ecd.jpg[/img]

v 0.1.06 - 2018.03.05
- Completely upgraded pathfinding system
- Completely reworked mob spawning system
- Can now walk on resources and stumps
- Fixed a bug related to long distance teleporting
- Changed obelisk sensing collider to a 0.5s sphere check

The system isn't perfect, nor does it need to be right now. There are seams between sectors that monsters can get hitched on, but not often, and especially not when chasing players. Monster and pig AI has been rewritten to accommodate the new system and still needs a bit of improvement and tweaking.

Ultimately this system will be much more universally available to all entities, friendly and not, making it easier for me to add in new monsters and NPCs which I hope to get into over the next couple days!

Mobs now also spawn statically per area, though they do not yet check for housing and player proximity so you may run into a monster when reloading a saved game, but this will be addressed today or tomorrow. It may be a bit difficult to level at the moment, but this too will change today or tomorrow with the addition of new content and some tweaks.

Sorry to keep everyone waiting until I could get this working, but it's a big improvement for my work flow. There is also now less of a "tick" to the game that some players were aware of, caused in part by the old pathfinding system that was constantly updating "nodes" on the main thread whenever you were moving around. Navigation map generation is now off the main thread and only happens in chunks of around 100m, mostly imperceptible.

notes.title: Weekly Update #6 2018.03.03
notes.content:
Coming at you on a Saturday night, this week was a busy one as I implemented a vastly improved pathfinding system. There are several methods to chose from and then several ways to go about using each of the methods, I'm working with the latest and greatest from Unity called navmesh. Navmesh isn't a new concept, nor new to Unity, but procedural runtime navmesh has only been officially implemented in the past six months and is still largely undocumented. That means there were a lot of questions that I had to figure out for myself and with other developers online, but everything is working very well. I'll be looking for feedback on the performance as there are different ways to go about many of the steps going on behind the scenes.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/17f4770e29b1eb8c1731ca928a6b3910340e9d14.jpg[/img]

Here we can see a monster that's gone up a ramp and two flights of stairs to get to our player.
This is important not only for general combat, animal pathing, and so forth, but also for town defence quests, and player summoned NPCs which I hope to be getting into next week.

The key binding system was also brought in since our last weekly update which is a big deal for player convenience. This is not a final solution for players in need of more controller support though and joystick axis are still on the todo list.

Coming in the next patch v0.1.06 alongside the new pathfinding we'll also be working with a very different mob and animal spawning system. Prior to v0.1.06 monsters just spawned continously around players and many made it clear it was very difficult to get things done in the higher levels. Solace Crafting is definitely aiming to become more of a building and crafting game than a fighting centered RPG, and the new system will certainly have monsters out and about but they won't be continously respawning for no reason. Next week I will try to reincorporate the first small "encounter," a small event with 1-3 monster guards that rewards light, experience, and possibly a reward.
Encounters of small, medium, and large sizes are intended to be the main sources of "combat" or adventure experience. Players can choose when to seek them out, and work on their adventuring abilities (the reason for the current tower placeholder system being important).

One subject we've been talking about on the forums this week is the way that rarities are handled in-game. Currently an uncommon tier 0 sword is better than a common tier 1 sword, giving reason for their existance, but all too quickly do they become backpack space-takers, out-classed by higher level materials. I'd like to propse a new system and get your opinion on it.
Say we still have rare nodes, but they do not drop readily usable rare resources. Instead the drop normal resources and a rarity essences. Say you've gather 25 uncommon essences mining teir 0 ore during your first few levels. You've just gathered and smelted your first 25 tier 1 ore and crafted a new breastplate to match your current level. Now you take you common breastplate to your enchanting table and you infuse it with your 25 uncommon essences (25 being required because it cost 25 ore to craft the breastplate) upgrading it from common tier 1 to uncommon tier 1. This would let you gather and hold onto your rare essences only using them when you are ready, on whatever level and tier you are able to.

Let me know what you think!

Thank you again for everyone participating in Early Access! Still only six weeks in and we've improved a lot of basic gameplay, graphics, and performance. There are still a lot of minor tweaks and options to be worked on, but I'm going to be trying to balance a mix of new content and general improvements starting next week now that the majority of serious problems have been dealt with.

notes.title: Beta v 0.1.05e
notes.content:
I'm still working on the improved pathfinding/mob spawning, but wanted to get some things up that we've been talking about.

I also wanted to mention that one of our most active players has uploaded several videos to YouTube, mostly for bug reporting purposes, that were flagged with copywrite infringement claims. Looking into it, there are automatic checks (audio/video recognition AI) that go through all YouTube content trying to make sure that content is not going against copywrite laws. In this case the AI has of course failed and I am in the process of disputing the false claims. Should anyone run into this in the future please rest assure I am always putting forth extra effort to be sure that we do everything legal and legitimate. All sounds and music used in-game are 100% paid for and can absolutely be uploaded and shared on YouTube. Never a dull week!

v 0.1.05e - 2018.02.27
- Fixed holding down attack not working
- Added autorun key (default is R )
- Pigs will now grant bonus meat on the last harvest
- Crafting and harvesting experience is now measured using non-whole numbers. Resources 3 or more tiers lower than your current profession level for said resource will grant no experience while 1 and 2 tiers under will grant reduced experience. Likewise resources tiered higher than your current profession level for said resource will grant increased experience. This shift will reset the experience at your current level for all professions, but not your profession levels.
- Crafting with and harvesting rare resources now grant increased experience per level of rarity
- Enchanting is no longer 5+ enchants per level, but grants 10 exp per basic enchant at equal tier, giving more or less the same results along with all of the new benefits applied to all professions and the way they gain experience
- Improved storm and heavy rain sound loops

You may need to restart Steam for the update to begin.

notes.title: Live update & beta patch v 0.1.05d
notes.content:
This patch brings the beta branch up to v 0.1.05d but I am pushing v 0.1.05c to the live build, as it has been found to be quite stable. The 0.1.05 series has divided characters and worlds and will require all players on the live build to start a new world. My apologies for that, but this system was put in place so that won't have to happen much more from here on.

Today I got well into implementing a better pathfinding system. Not so long ago Unity's pathfinding system was incompatible with runtime generation, forcing games like Solace Crafting to work with third party software, as we currently do. Recently that has changed and I've managed to get it working almost entirely off of the main thread, which means it doesn't affect framerate. When this is in and working it will allow fully three dimensional pathfinding so that monsters can find their way up towers and ramps and just navigate better than they are currently in general.
When this goes in I will mostly likely add in some limitations to player movement as well. Currently we can run at full speed almost straight up the steepest mountain cliffs. This makes is unfairly easy to get away from monsters, as well as just unrealistic in general. Hopefully in the future we will have climbing with nice animations for those extra tricky to reach spots.

Once the new pathfinding is in I've got a lot in store for monsters, towns, and NPCs! Thank you again to everyone participating in early access!

The changes to the live build are as follows:

v 0.1.05c - 2018.02.22
- Fixed an error where obelisks could get stuck on elemental corpses
- Obelisks will no longer show damage above the hotkeys
- Obelisk kills will no longer reward exp
- Enabled beacon upgrades on solaces
- Added a timer on monster audio playback to keep them from spamming
- Finished keybinding code. Only "Hold to walk" can be shift or alt or control. The rest will treat shift, control, and alt keys as combinations.
- Added disable analytics setting
- Added always run setting
- Added hide helmet setting
- Fixed swimming
- Fixed ambient volume not loading properly on the start screen
- Added notifications on the character creation screen that colors and equipment are for reference only
- Carrots, cabbages, and dropped items will no longer collide with players
- Removed carrot and cabbage rarities (these were capable of changing based on distance from camera and as such won't happen anymore)
- Changed "interact" checks to gauge multiple items based on distance to player. Dropped items inside of objects should now be retrievable depending on the direction they are interacted with.
- Fixed tree billboard colors
- Added numbers to the hotkeys
- Added colored borders to inventory and equipment slots (others (facilities, etc) are being rewritten to use the same base code)
- Rewrote inventory slots to be able to add more slots for bags and things in the future
- Added "T" to the tier display on inventory and equipment slots and turned display on for all item types
- Started adding key binding options in the in-game control menu. Beware this is partially incomplete! Only the W A S D keys are currently changable. The logic is all there and will be finished early tomorrow.
- Delete world button now works
- Turned of the character and world "edit" button "..." until I get it working
- Delete for both world and characters now send to the recycle bin instead of instantly erasing
- Added a warning for when trying to create a world with the same name of an existing world
- Fixed a mob related memory leak
- Added a check against reports of higher level mobs following players through teleports
- Fixed attack speed increase bug
- Fixed harvest tool speeds (bare hands: 3, stone: 2.5, metal: 2 base)
- Fixed tool tiers decreasing speed instead of increasing it
- Fixed a rare weather error during loading
- Fixed T1+ new structures not always placing their first foundation
- Buildings can now intersect with the ground
- Buildings can no longer be built underground
- Foundations can now be built if "attached" to other buildings, or ground
- Fixed "You have been awarded 6 adventuring points" in chat on startup
- Fixed "+*** light" in chat on startup
- Smoothed the warning and damage message box edges
- Fixed a bug where a saved area with zero dropped items would not overwrite the savefile with dropped items, causing them to reload after being picked up
- Separated and fixed player save version and world save version displays
- Fixed teleport/recall putting you up one floor when present
- Improved water blending
- Improved underwater
- Reduced terrain resolution
- Finished adding in a number of missing stat/attribute math variables/equations
- Fixed basic attacks and harvests not altering speed based on stats
- Punching now has a base speed of 3 and uses attributes to calc damage and speed
- Harvesting tools now have individual speeds that decrease with tier/rarity (only newly crafted tools)
- Added a harvesting and crafting tabs to the stats interface and populated the harvesting tab
- Turned off "you have unlocked tier" facility messages
- Added a total resources gatherered counter for all professions (not exposed yet)
- Fixed unrelated materials leveling up professions during crafting
- Fixed harvesting profession variables not saving properly
- Leveling up all crafting and harvesting professions should correctly require tiered materials equivalent to the professions current level/tier.
- Added level next to profession title in crafting recipe details interface
- Fixed snow going black
- Improved and sped up swimming in all directions
- Limited maximum monster size and speed
- Fixed monster agro range scaling with monster size
- Separated souls and worlds. This should allow souls to be carried throughout all game versions from here on.
- Added cloud quality controls

The beta patch notes are as follows:

v 0.1.05d - 2018.02.23
- Enabled hardware mouse
- Fixed bad string in enchanting interface
- Fixed enchanting not leveling up properly
- Gave stone foundations a proper PBR texture
- Improved solace and solace beacon shader to render fog and glow at night
- Fixed several terraforming bugs
- Fixed grass not moving with terraforming
- Rain will no longer fall through buildings
- Fixed some solace upgrade interface bugs. Perhaps not all of them
- Fixed door animations

notes.title: Weekly Update #5 2018.02.19
notes.content:
It was a rough weekend! I was really looking forward to continuing with volumetric lighting and fog, but they ended up bringing in way too many problems, one of which I can't easily solve without at least a couple more days of work, which at this point is really not worth it. Some day in the months to come I will revisit the problem and get it working, but there is a lot more than needs attention right now.

While trying various tricks to get things to work I did pour over a ton of code, making improvements, and in general optimizing the overall orginzation of the code to use more global variables, making it much easier to test and control things. We are back on the dual camera system now with simple fog.

There were a variety of bugs in v 0.1.04 that players were diligently and generously reporting. A fair share of those were specific to me trying to squeeze better graphics in, and should be back to working normal. There are still a number of smaller problems, I will be on top of shortly. My apologies for not being very active on the forums or chat the past three days. I know it's a bit draining when things don't feel like they're improving on the beta branch. Shame on me for fussing about the graphics in my honest opinion. Back to gameplay and content!

Beta participators will almost certainly need to start a new world, and I will probably need to force it to v 0.1.05 tomorrow afternoon, meaning worlds created anew now will work, but bugged worlds from v0.1.04 will no longer be loadable, though I doubt they're very playable now.

I hope it's warming up for everyone in the northern hemisphere as it is here, despite the wind. Thank you again for participating in early access!

- Fixed tower (encounter) position management problems
- Fixed teleport/recall putting you up one floor when present
- Improved water blending
- Improved underwater (wip)
- Increased terrain size
- Reduced terrain resolution

You may need to restart Steam for the update to begin.

To opt into Beta you need to go to your Steam Library, right-click on Solace Crafting, select Properties, click on the Beta tab, and opt-in to the beta.

notes.title: Beta v 0.1.04
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/200011e8d1dff1c55cfcf3c986418936a7345f41.jpg[/img]
The biggest changes in this patch are under the hood and not obvious to the player, but removing the second camera took most of Tuesday and Wednesday, and still needs some visual work. It's visual quality work so I'm going to put it off for a bit to get some more fixes and requested features in. The biggest benefit of this change is the high quality atmpsheric controls this allows. We now have volumetric lighting and advanced fog in-game which makes the worlds much prettier, and much more realistic. I have the fog distance turned up pretty high because the draw range settings go up to 48km, but I will try linking them to far draw range settings in the future and see how that works. Sun and moon shafts are in but not turned on for this patch until I can get buttons in for them, probably tomorrow.
(check the in-game settings to turn atmopsheric on)

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/d1fbade8214e8fa22610153cb3c3df211da799fc.jpg[/img]
The second big change is that now souls and worlds are completely separated. This means that you can create a new soul and have it travel between different worlds, or create several souls to play in one world, and so on. The largest benefit of this approach is that now when worlds need to be wiped because of bigger changes, we won't have to wipe our characters as well. You should even be able to bring in old saves, though their "world" files will remain on your hard disk (underneath the character folder) they won't be used anymore.
In the future I will look into building a system to try and "upgrade" world saves from previous versions. There are some unavoidable problems that will come with that, but it still beats losing everything. Perhaps even before that, there will also be options for saving and loading buildings; not really an alternative to wipes, you'd still need the materials, but that's always been a planned feature and isn't far off.

That ate up almost all of my first three days full-time, but are both things I really wanted to get in quite some time ago. Starting tomorrow I'm going to be grinding through the todo list for a while, key bindings, bugs, and so on, so that we can move closer to getting more buildings and monsters and things in!

I think I smoothed the starting area out a bit too much, and it feels like there are too few mountains now, let me know what you guys/gals think though. Sub-world travel (dimensions) could be finished very easy now, it's pretty tempting to throw together some elemental planes, but we'll stick to the development plan for now =]

Thank you again to everyone participating in early access and especially to everyone in beta!

notes.title: Patch v 0.1.03d
notes.content:
Due to several bugs in the live build I am pushing this patch to both Beta and Live versions of Solace Crafting.

I didn't quite finish the big patch I'm working on so it will probably be tomorrow. It may bring up some new problems, and will be on the Beta branch. Amidst working on that, I may have turned something on or off inadvertantly... I wanted to get trashbins and the smoothed starting area up today though.

As for new "world" versions (changes to terrain generation usually) requiring players to start over, this actually only requires the world to start over, not players. I'm thinking of several different approaches of minimizing this as it will still happen many times to come:

1. We can allow characters to "move" into a new version, bringing their inventory, equipment, and everything they've learned with them. Only the buildings and things they've built will need to be remade. This is viable for almost all patches, and eventually I should be able to set it up so that characters can move between different worlds even of different versions in most cases. We could also just put "Characters" and "Worlds" into entirely different categories and require players to select one of each on the loading screen. This would preseve character in almost all cases.

2.
