notes.title: Weekly Update #4 2018.02.12
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/1ab5f58438f267fa427f11d40fdd9b39c89057cc.jpg[/img]

Roughly six years ago someone I knew put a game on Steam. It wasn't just "someone else," it was someone whose house I had been to as a child, who grew up in more or less the same environment as I did. I lost my excuse for not getting into game development, which up to that point had seemed "out of my league." But I was not a game developer. I had no formal education in the subject and of course no professional experience either, nor did I need them. I had 30 years of gamer frustration, and a fierce belief that I could do better.

I started out writing in notebooks what I thought made games fun, and what a game would be like if I were to make it. I watched tutorial videos on programming for hours every night. I made, and remade voxel engines and mesh generators over and over. After years of trial and error I had a rough outline for a game I knew others like me could enjoy, I only needed to make it.

I'm inclined here to say "unfortunately, I spent almost a year and half trying to work social media and crowdfunding campaigns in my favor," but I'm confident the experience I gained from that time was necessary and will serve me well in the years to come.

Today I punched my time card for the last time at my job as a CAD Operator in the manufacturing industry. Tomorrow I start my first day as a Game Developer, and Owner of Big Kitty Games. It was a long road, full of strangers and kindness and coffee, lot's of coffee.

Over the next 5 months I hope to improve Solace Crafting into a stable and robust game worthy of increased sales. I hope to in time generate enough revenue to put together a small team of dedicated developers, so that we can bring Solace Crafting to a level of performance and content that it would take me years to achieve on my own. My long term goals for Solace Crafting are many and we've got a lot to do even before version 1.0, but the path is clearly defined and I am ready.

Tomorrow is day one.

notes.title: Beta v0.1.03
notes.content:
I have opened up a Beta branch that will allow players to choose to play the latest version, as opposed to sticking to whatever the latest "stable" version is. This is intended to limit the stress on new players when new features are added in that bring in unexpected bugs.

v 0.1.03 - 2018.02.10
- Fixed the building layout still showing after toggling it off then on again
- Fixed and turned on world repositioning. This will recenter the world every 8km to prevent floating point percision errors. It's pretty sticky stuff and may bring up some new bugs. The sun and sky don't seem to reposition with it properly just yet. Keep in mind that's 8km X or Z, not X + Z so you can be more than 8km away from the start without necessarily triggering a shift.
- Changed terrain generation noise functions to be smoother over long distances removing the sharps chunks that would show up quite frequently. This requires a new save.

In order to download the beta version you only need to go to your Steam Library, right-click on Solace Crafting then click Properties. There should be a Beta tab, allowing you to switch between the "stable" build and the beta build. That means you can play saves from v 0.1.02 if you revert to the stable build.

You may need to restart Steam if you have already opted into the beta and the patch does not begin. Or opt out and back in.

notes.title: Weekly Update #3 2018.02.06
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/c14064114e2c0657516dd3ea809d9faee220ede5.jpg[/img]

Coming at you a couple days late, I've had a busy weekend working to increase performance. This latest patch v.0.1.02m brings back our fancy vegetation system with vast improvements on performance. I've also started setting up customization settings so players can tweak and tune their settings to better fit their systems, after which the current "quality" settings will turn into recommendations. Until an interface with knobs and sliders are setup there are three new commands /quality 0, /quality 1, and /quality 2 that will change the quality settings in-game to any of the presets, 0 being Fast, 1 being Good, and 2 being Fantastic. I hope the performance is as increased for everyone's systems as it is for mine. I like to run in fantastic even at a lower framerate, but can run steadily over 100 on fast on my not-so-hot system.

Only four days left at my day job, the last being Monday of next week. Starting Tuesday I will be here full-time pushing the envelope!

Tomorrow I will be trying to setup a development build for players to opt into and push larger changes to that before pushing them live. The first big patch planned for tomorrow will remove the invisible wall at 15km out, letting players travel infinitely into the wilds! Stuff gets pretty big out there though, don't say I didn't warn you!

Thank you again to everyone that has bought a copy of Solace Crafting in this early stage, and especially to all the dedicated bug reporters helping me find things I never would have on my own!

Here are the latest patch notes:
v 0.1.02m - 2018.02.06
- Added invincibility during teleportation and world loading to prevent the possibility of starving, freezing, and generally dying before the world loads
- Returned the more robust vegetation system with performance improvements. Though still a work in progress, the framerate is better than the "standard" approach in v0.1.02l. Please let me know how it works for everyone.
- Reduced the overall amount of types of trees for increased performance, resulting in somewhat less trees overall
- Carrots and cabbages are now resources meaning they can spawn in tiers and rarities and are harvested not just picked up
- Harvesting now checks for resource collision using a line straight out of the camera measuring distance from the player instead of a sphere check in front of the player
- Fixed harvesting speed passives not working
- Changed the way enchanting tables are saved. Not sure if that's what's causing "stuck" tables yet.
- Added /quality 0, /quality 1, and /quality 2 commands to change video quality in-game until I can setup some buttons
- Fixed clouds not rendering in quality 0 (Fast)
- Fixed jump looping

You may need to restart Steam for the download to begin.

notes.title: Hotfix v 0.1.02i
notes.content:
Due to some players experiencing very poor performance and even crashing I have removed the vegetation control system that was managing trees, grass, resources, and other flora. It really wasn't designed for a procedural open world like we have and was sending way too many instructions to video cards. In it's place I have reverted to a much more common system that doesn't look as good (especially grass) but runs fine even in big procedural environments.

This also fixes the lack of difference between the quality modes available on launch. Regardless of quality the vegetation system was bogging everything down. Now Fast runs much faster than Good, and Good much faster than Fantastic. That's around 170fps, 80fps, and 35fps for me on my Radeon GTX 450 which is by no means a high class graphics card nowadays.

As usual I don't want to force a new save game on anyone, but as the vegetation has been completely reworked any areas you may have "cleared" of resources may have resource back in them as the resources of the entire world will be regenerated as if a new game has been started. So you may have a tree in your house, and it might be awesome, or you can cut it down.

The grass is ugly, I hate it, it's one of my pet peeves, it will be improved. Tree stumps, flowers, and some other things are temporarily missing as well, but everything will make it back in much more performant. Resource LODs (draw distances) are quite low at the moment as well, I will be readjusting them.

I have also uploaded a 64 bit version of the game. My apologies that I'm not 100% sure how Steam handles that, but I think you will need to uninstall and reinstall for the x64 version to reach you. Steam should be able to recognize that your system is x32 or x64 and both versions are marked to be 'only' applicable for their appropriate systems, even though technically x64 can run x32. If you have a 1GB update, then Steam has automatically updated to the x64 bit version for you! I was unable to double-check as the developer it provides me a separate package.

I value gameplay and stability over graphics and flare. I'm sorry for the ups and downs over the past few days!

v 0.1.02i - 2018.02.03
- Fixed vSync option
- Temporarily replaced vegetation/resource control systems with a much more performant style
- Added 64 bit version

You may need to restart Steam for the download to begin and/or reinstall to upgrade to 64 bit. If you don't know whether you are on a 64 bit system you can right click on "My Computer" (Windows 7) or "This PC" (Windows 10) in the Explorer and click "Properties"

Happy Gaming!

So you may have a tree in your house, and it might be awesome, or you can cut it down.

The grass is ugly, I hate it, it's one of my pet peeves, it will be improved. Tree stumps, flowers, and some other things are temporarily missing as well, but everything will make it back in much more performant. Resource LODs (draw distances) are quite low at the moment as well, I will be readjusting them.

I have also uploaded a 64 bit version of the game. My apologies that I'm not 100% sure how Steam handles that, but I think you will need to uninstall and reinstall for the x64 version to reach you. Steam should be able to recognize that your system is x32 or x64 and both versions are marked to be 'only' applicable for their appropriate systems, even though technically x64 can run x32. If you have a 1GB update, then Steam has automatically updated to the x64 bit version for you! I was unable to double-check as the developer it provides me a separate package.

I value gameplay and stability over graphics and flare. I'm sorry for the ups and downs over the past few days!

- Fixed vSync option
- Temporarily replaced vegetation/resource control systems with a much more performant style
- Added 64 bit version

You may need to restart Steam for the download to begin and/or reinstall to upgrade to 64 bit. If you don't know whether you are on a 64 bit system you can right click on "My Computer" (Windows 7) or "This PC" (Windows 10) in the Explorer and click "Properties"

Happy Gaming!

notes.title: Hotfix v 0.1.02g
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/8be5e22d3e665e5ddc412ed2e2a30ff2bef4f2fb.jpg[/img]

Beautification techniques are not really what I'm lookig to spend time on, but in upgrading some things to take care of old bugs, sometimes the improvements are more than just functional! The above shot is a sneak peak at what will be out soon!

I'm still working on finishing up the environment improvements, mostly because I want to make sure everyone has total control over them to turn things on and off. While implementing things (kicking them until they work) I came up with some decent improvements, one of which is going to take a little extra work. To go along with all of these changes I'm going to add in the better noise which gets rid of those pointy ridges that show up at seemingly random parts of the landscape. This will me a save game wipe =[

Most of these are small steps towards turning the 15km walls off again and letting people run as far as they like! Still a few more steps and things to do, but not far out now. =]

I spent most of today looking into increasing performance. Rendering the terrains is bar far the most taxing part of the game. There are major improvements down the road, a big set of which is still under development by one of the genius programmers whose tools I make use of. In the meantime, giving players the option to turn down the draw distance is back in and you can see what works best for your computer setup. Currently terrains are brought in in 512m sections, which causes a bit of a stagger, mostly when their collider is brought into the game engine, I'm looking into slicing that up further and spreading the generation of multiple terrains across more frames.

Thank you again to everyone participating in early access! I'm sorry I still have a week and a half at my day job before I can really grind through the remaining bugs and wanted features list.

Not a ton in this patch on the foreground, but a fair amount of changes behind the scenes. notes.title: Weekly Update #2 2018.01.28
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/78fef263e4df4d1f40cd4e35c615e09f66c6dca9.jpg[/img]

The majority of bugs have been squashed! Yay! The big ones anyway. There are still some crafting station and refining station bugs lingering about and a few rare occurances I'm hard at work repairing.

Some of the crash logs that I received from players were showing indications of 3rd party software in use causing problems, so I set out to update and better manage the tools that I use. The first step was adding version control to each of them which let's me see and control what gets updated to be sure all of my customization doesn't get overwritten. This has indeed done away with some of the bugs, as well as improved visuals and performance! Clouds and fog in particular are looking extra gorgeous.

I'm still finishing up the last of the integration work and am not quite ready to patch it in tonight.

On a side note I've fixed the unnatural bumpiness that seems to show up on terrains around the shore and often in the mountains. Revisiting work on the terrains however will require me to force another wipe, so I've put it off for a little later when I can get around to adding more detail to the biomes, maybe even bringing deserts back in! Then we can get some more flavored monsters in their rightful places =]

Thank you again to everyone participating in early access! Still only 11 days in, and me with my full-time job for another two weeks, but things are coming along nicely! I hope I haven't frustrated anyone too much! You have all been very kind and understanding putting up with my current schedule.

I'll be back tomorrow!
Happy gaming!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/dda259201b9b79ec5c20ed44a318dbbf14636e27.jpg[/img]

This patch overhauls the damage and armor mechanics throughout all levels. I'm not forcing players to start a new game but be warned that equipment crafted before the patch will be quite overpowered. notes.title: Hotfix v 0.1.01e
notes.content:
This patch fixes a lot of problems in regards to tiered and rare resources. It also moves the camera to a locked mouse follow. This was requested by more than a few and really it feels a lot better to me this way. Let me know what you think. If there is a need for it I can put the old camera controls back in as an optional mode.

The daily amount of posts on the forums and e-mails in my inbox is increasing! My apologies if any of my responses come off as short or if I don't reply personally.

v 0.1.01e - 2018.01.23
- Changed the camera to a fixed mouse follow
- The menu is now opened using the Escape key and will close other windows
- Empty chat messages will no longer print a black line with player name
- Lowered starting platform
- Fixed T1+ facilities reverting to T0 on placement
- Fixed refining facility upgrade costs spending equally tiered resources
- Fixed refining facility UI not updating after an upgrade
- Added steepness check to ground torch placement
- Fixed resource tier generation, as it was indeed not working as expected. This was also affecting node rarity, should have more rare nodes now. 
- Fixed and changed resource tier determination a little
  0 - 4km = 100% T0
  4 - 5km = 90% T0, 10% T1
  5 - 6km = 10% T0, 90% T1
  6 - 9km = 100% T1 and so on
- Reduced rare tree node spawn chance by 10% because they're so abundant
- Increased rare pig spawn chance by 10% because they're so few
- Fixed an error not dropping items properly
- Fixed instances of hotkeys remaining active during rename and chat input
- Fixed the start a new structure UI so that tiers and resources can be selected

notes.title: Early access begins!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/2cfc3feea5b46dbd726e20db88a65b80b7ed1445.jpg[/img]

Already there is love and hate from all directions, making my stomach ache and my heart race! That's why I started this tough, people are upset! I was long upset at how big teams of developers could produce so little after so much time and money was given to them.

I can't demand anyone's trust and can only ask that you be honest with yourself. If you don't have 15$ to spend on buying a game that is still very much just a "potential" then do not buy it. Give me a couple months to prove to you that I am actively developing this, that I am listening to players, that I am interested in content and gameplay, and above all that I'm human, an amateur, and have a lot left to learn.

I've never sold a game on Steam. I don't know if I'll sell 10 copies or 10,000 in a day or a week or a year. If there is money to be had though it goes into hiring artists and programmers to improve Solace Crafting, not some side-project.

This week I am here full-time, and in another few weeks I will be here every week, full-time, doing my best! That's all that I've got!

Please be aware of the suggested system requirements. I don't have any lower end machines to test things on, and am not sure how 3-4 year old video cards will handle things.

It all starts here!

Happy Gaming!

Malkere
Big Kitty Games

notes.title: Darkness and light. Patch v0.0.21
notes.content:
Darkness and light

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/d4d05bd9759ba458d8444f325bbf11b324aa5cc1.jpg[/img]

( As posted on [url=https://www.patreon.com/posts/16269657]Patreon[/url] )

When developing a game there are a lot of choices that come into play if you look at the whole picture. Animation, scripting, and dozens of other professions within what we call "game development" each can take decades to master and are constantly evolving. As a solo developer (for the time being) it's tough keeping up on any one profession, but dabbling in all of them can be very rewarding.
One thing in Solace Crafting that has not had much attention given to it yet is lighting. This past week I got in the first workings of wall and ground torches letting us setup our own sources of light. To "celebrate" this, I've made the nighttime much darker.

Ultimately I want to give much more control over lightning to players via spells, trinkets, achievements and so forth, but for now I've just added a magically permanent light to all players. Because no really, it's dark out there. I also plan to add sometime hopefully in the next two weeks the ability to color not only equipment and buildings, but torches, and player bound lights as well.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/af8e3447dc1b80dbcfff6ee9793cd911c2ab009b.jpg[/img]

Besides lighting, one of the main components of the inventory system, what I call inventory slots, got a complete overhaul. The method I was using involved a master script trying to control all forms of inventory. These can be player equipment, player inventory, forge inventory, monster drops, treasure chests, and many other things capable of producing and storing items of all kinds. As the system grew the master script trying to be all capable was getting uglier and uglier.

Instead, now I have reworked the system to allow inventory slots to talk to one another and attend to their own needs. This way an inventory slot knows what it's capable of, for example a leg equipment slot can only accept leg armor, and only at or lower than the player's level, and if it's full it has to be able to take off what's already equipped, and so on. There is a lot of hidden logic that goes into running simple things like this that we players are used to and I'm not looking to cut corners.

Of course, for now just getting things to work properly is more important than everything working perfectly as quite a lot is still in motion and changing over time.

I plan to start making things more and more dangerous as I start implementing building damage (not building destruction), more monsters, and improving the solace upgrade/town defense quests.

Hopefully by mid-February I'll start developing full-time! Taking what is now a great start to an open world fantasy survival RPG, and turning into a full fledged content rich experience full of monsters, towns, bosses, and achievements!

I declare 2018 the year of Solace Crafting! (for me anyway =)
The year my dreams come true!
Thank you for your patronage and I wish excitement and happiness your way as well!

Full patch notes:
v 0.0.21 - 2018.01.07
- Made nighttime much darker
- Added a light to players until we are able to equip a light source
- Fixed more inventory bugs, particularly refining stations refining stuff in player inventory
- Refining high tier resources now requires higher tier fuels
- Right-clicking an item while a facilitiy windows is open will now attemp to move the item
  (won't auto-stack yet / still not working in some cases)
- Right-clicking a piece of equipment will now try to equip it
- Right-clicking a consumable in your inventory will now attempt to eat it
- Improved 'right-click to place one' to work everywhere
- Hotbar skills can now be removed by clicking and dragging them off
- Combined all UI refresh calls into single passes
- Added lots of item icons
Building----------------------
- Stopped furniture placement dummy duplicates
- Fixed furniture placement mode not turning off in some cases
Adventuring----------------------
- Added icons for Disciple skills
Harvesting----------------------
- Fixed harvesting skill point display/saving/loading
- Added a harvesting ability for each profession
- Fixed passive harvesting skills
- Added icons for all harvesting skills
- Increased amount required to level harvesting professions (still need to make it visible)
- Added resource node rarities (uncommon, rare, elite, legendary)
  Rare cannot show up until tier 2, elite until tier 4, legendary until tier 6
  Each rarity is tougher than its lessers
- Changed uncommon+ loot drop logic on resources
- Added uncommon+ resource drop chances to all rarities
Crafting----------------------
- Rare items are now crafted using uncommon+ resources instead of blessings
- Locked refining facility craftable tiers to harvesting profession levels.

notes.title: v 0.0.20 is live!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/c14064114e2c0657516dd3ea809d9faee220ede5.jpg[/img]

I've set the release date to January 16, 2018! Let's hope I don't piss anyone off =] I have a fair share of days off between now and then, and only a few key features left I want to be sure to get in for a good Early Access feel. Then hopefully I will be able to focus on development full-time, or even better, higher a real programmer! =]>

Today's update got pushed back and back and back, but it brings in some great changes! Mainly that teleportation and floating point correction had been causing problems for a long time. It all seems to be fixed now but still needs to be tested often and repeatedly to squeeze out those smaller bugs that always try to hide.

notes.content:
Refining stations, crafting stations, new early game progression, and lots of little fixes as we push towards improved AI, and NPC summoning... I'm starting to eye that early access "release" button!

Check out a better description over at [url=https://www.patreon.com/solacecrafting]Patreon[/url]!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/e9f6dfe669cf47db5e128b33f414ad88b6c9f34a.jpg[/img]

v 0.0.18 - 2017.11.21
- This update will not accept older save files. Sorry!
- Replaced built-in "splash screen" with custom company logo screen in lieu of bug reports
- Fixed a building rotation bug, still seeing another though
- Fixed an error when clicking on the drop button
- Added several icons
- Improved monster hit registry on slopes
- Added a min/max body temperature indicator in the stats display
Harvesting:
- Changed resource rare rewards to be calculated per amount harvested not per swing
- Changed cloth to stalk(raw) and thread(refined)
- Changed leather to hide(raw) and leather(refined) (will get an animal in next update)
- Changed wood to timber(raw) and lumber(refined)
- Added resource processing facilities:
  Retting Vat: stalk -> thread. Uses globe of water as fuel
  Tanning Rack: hide -> leather. Uses tannin as fuel
  Sawing Station: timber -> lumber. No fuel required
  Forge: ore -> metal. Uses timber as fuel
- Changed resource processing user interface. One fuel is used per stack refined.
- Upgrades (tier upgrade for starters) are not in yet
Crafting:
- Fixed ingredient details not showing up in recipe details interface
- Fixed recipe list scroll sensitivity
- Changed recipe list ingredient displays to dynamic strings
- Fixed being able to craft higher level items than profession level when changing selected recipe
- Added "simple" cloth, tool, and club recipes that do not require processed resources
- Some items such as torch, and campfire are also classified as simple, meaning they have no level, tier, nor rarity
- Improved item details and recipe settings to not show/allow control of levels, tiers, nor rarity for simple items
- Improved item details to not show levels on tier only items such as resources, refining stations, and crafting stations
- Improved item details to color titles based on rarity
- Added Tailoring, Leatherworking, Smithing, Woodworking, and Stonecutting crafting stations (better models pending). The crafting interface will show if a crafting station is necessary, what tier is necessary, and if those requirements are being met or not. (will give crafting stations an interface with specific recipe lists/profession details in the future, leaving the profession/recipe browser separate from the actual crafting interface)
- Added craftable infinite fuel sources: water font, tannin font, and fire font for retting, tanning, and smelting. (these will require unlocking in the future)
- Facility tiers are not yet locked because they are not yet unlockable
Temperature, Thirst, Hunger:
- Changed the radial displays to lines with numbers

notes.title: v0.0.15 - Terraforming!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/fde4c15db8e7bebf089a4c0b1b935cc5a0f1fee3.jpg[/img]

Terraforming is live! With a very easy to follow interface, not unlike the building interface, terraforming land is easy! This is still just the first step in making this into a much better system of course. For now we are adjusting points, though in time I will implement edges and faces as well so you can go square by square instead of corner by corner.

One feature added that I also love is the ability to raise and lower a new buildings height relative to the ground. Normally in games the first block will stick very close to the floor causing it to get buried as soon as you move in some directions. With this freedom to shift anywhere between 5cm to 150cm we're able to take much better control. In time I will also implement rotation using z and c so you don't have to try and take baby steps to find just the right place.

v 0.0.15 - 2017.11.10
- Reduced trees a lot
- Reduced grass a bit
- Added /stuck command in case you fall through the world or get stuck
- Reworked start screen with up to date shaders and vegetation (WIP)
Building:
- Stopped building interface movement colliding with player
- Q and E now raise and lower foundations when selecting a new building area
Solaces:
- Solace storage is now limited by the amount of solaces built and their storage upgrades
- Turned on solace storage upgrades
Terraforming:
- Added terraforming interface, WASD to move, QE to raise/lower (creative mode style for now)

notes.title: v0.0.13 patch notes
notes.content:
This patch brings in the new foliage system, a big improvement that comes with lots of little fixes to the flora and resources of the game world. In late October the terrain system will be reworked into a different system I'm working on, fixing the minor graphical errors still seen sometimes between near and distant terrains, along with lots of improvements.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/f06b4b6660cf9d27d002709382ff02d34ce4c409.jpg[/img]

Tomorrow I'll be making some well needed changes to building I hope to patch before the day ends.

v 0.0.13 - 2017.09.30
- Complete rework of foliage system, fixing many harvesting bugs
  (Biomes are still being reworked)
- Fixed spells not using mana
- Spells now base damage off equipped weapon, like melee and ranged do
- Fixed facility, building, and dropped item saving/loading problems
  (Still seeing some problems on Dimension Crystals over 8km out)
- Added model for dropped items
- Added recognition for tutorial quest steps being finished early
- Fixed health/energy/mana refilling on equipment changes/reloading

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/029eefc4560193d1d99af35627c4daf1ff7bd6ff.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Solace Crafting - Now live on Kickstarter!
notes.content:
The press release just went out! Social Media campaigns are revving their engines. I'm hoping to make this my life and duty for years to come and it all starts right now!

[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/bigkittygames/solace-crafting-distance-based-fantasy-survival-rp]Join our backers![/url]

Click above and check out the new video further detailing my recent progress.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/be5bbcd53baf4de2f29f3a7021bb08c5adaf7866.jpg[/img]

We pushed the release back a ways to get out of game convention air space, but we've put the ball in motion now!

How can you help?
Yes you! You can be a huge help by sharing our campaign on Steam, social media, or e-mailing friends and family who love to game or love to support a good cause! Each share can generate over a thousand views!

[url=http://www.twitter.com/solacecrafting/]Solace Crafting on Twitter[/url]
[url=http://www.facebook.com/solacecrafting/]Solace Crafting on Facebook[/url]
[url=http://www.instagram.com/solacecrafting/]Solace Crafting on Instagram[/url]

Lot's of new updates coming out over the next month as we push our reach as far as we can.

Funding or not we'll make the dream come true.
With funding though, we'll get there ten times faster!

Fall is in the air! Stay warm out there!

notes.title: First wave of closed testing has begun!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/af3ff23098a2fefe09751fb7ac1d87b9947580af.jpg[/img]

It's been an extremely busy past few weeks. We've been approved by Steam for release when we are ready. New artwork is up! A press release is scheduled to go out any day. Kickstarter is less than two weeks out. And I've got a few close testers trying Solace Crafting out in its current state (quite shabby) on different machines.

The goal at this point is still first and foremost to acquire the minimum funding required for me to focus on Solace Crafting full time and get enough content in for public players to not feel let down by their purchase. All in all we hope to grow for years to come with lots and lots of crafting survival PvE content, but the ball is definitely rolling at full speed now!

A few more patches and the demo will be ready for public release as well letting the character creation contest begin!

Be sure to join the [url=https://storage.googleapis.com/solacecrafting/mailinglist.html]mailing list![/url]

More news is just around the corner!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/13cc421ab61538ddc566bb3caa52ddd5485a8e79.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Upcoming Character Studio Contest
notes.content:
[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/2305c4f3b6c5776f74ed9ed2b5e2edce082811f3.jpg][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/c38c623ad0e7e8eae46a94ac0b5090a1278b2144.jpg[/img][/url]
Character customization is a core aspect of almost all features in Solace Crafting. The first step, avatar creation, isn't something you may do that often, but it can have a huge impact on your experience for the rest of the game. To make sure that players can be silly, sexy, studly, ugly, or whatever they're interested in role-playing I've been working on a Character Studio with a lot of different dimensions of choice.

In hopes of raising excitement for our upcoming Kickstarter (Sept. 5th) I will be releasing a stand-alone build of the Character Studio for download and hosting a series of contests to see who can take the silliest, the uglies, and the most beautiful screenshots; with prizes of course!

Be sure to join the mailing list
http://www.solacecrafting.com/mailinglist.html
To get a notification when things start hitting the fan!

[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/c1f589856d9a70e13cfda96c72212a55da7c837d.jpg][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/3f3bdf433fc15cd47ff34f63c78a64785d702268.jpg[/img][/url] [url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/bbb228da504aaa3a0a2c26324edef2625409f759.jpg][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/ff8cb9a00995a2cf7be4e402b5229eacf1707a46.jpg[/img][/url]

On a side note, I plan to let players reshape their characters post-creation instead of locking their choices in for all of eternity. Sometimes your mood changes, you know? ːsteamhappyː
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29537945/1c1db30930747d217f9d5057fcf6f28a206f54cd.jpg[/img]

notes.title: It's great to be here!
notes.content:
It's great to be on Steam! Soon we will be on Kickstarter as well! The goal being to raise enough money to go full time so I can polish and launch a solid alpha build worthy of Steam before the end of the year.

I'm eyeballs deep in code setting up procedural towns, dangerous encounters, underground mysteries, and more. Give us a follow or add us to your wishlist to keep informed on when our Kickstarter starts, and when we release on Steam.

Thank you!
